name: Neuromuscular Disease with Dilated Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Neuromuscular Disease with Dilated Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Echocardiographic or MRI evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
Clinical evidence of proximal muscle weakness and/or electromyographic findings consistent with myopathy
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with neuromuscular disease and dilated cardiomyopathy (e.g., LMNA, DES, DMD)
Family history of neuromuscular disease or cardiomyopathy
Elevated serum creatine kinase levels indicating muscle damage

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical neuromuscular weakness and confirmed dilated cardiomyopathy with either genetic confirmation or supportive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is strongly recommended to confirm diagnosis and guide management.

searchTerms: gradual weakness in upper legs and arms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
searchTerms: enlarged heart with poor pumping function
dilated cardiomyopathy with low ejection fraction
heart muscle disease causing weak contractions

common.symptomName: Arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia
searchTerms: fast irregular heartbeats like AF or VT

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion due to heart failure

laboratory: Elevated cardiac biomarkers (e.g., BNP, troponin) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing dilated left ventricle with reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and dilation
Muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration and muscle atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in LMNA, DES, DMD, or other related genes
other: Muscle biopsy showing dystrophic or myopathic changes
Electrocardiogram abnormalities including conduction defects and arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: No pathogenic mutations in neuromuscular disease genes
History of ischemic heart disease or toxic exposures
Lack of dilated cardiomyopathy on imaging
Different genetic mutations (e.g., DMD without cardiac phenotype)

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
Severe respiratory muscle weakness causing hypoventilation
references: Orphanet: Neuromuscular Disease with Dilated Cardiomyopathy (ORPHA:217610)
Towbin JA, et al. Dilated Cardiomyopathy: Genetic Determinants and Mechanisms. Circ Res. 2019.
Mercuri E, et al. Diagnosis and management of neuromuscular disorders with cardiac involvement. Nat Rev Cardiol. 2020.
